title: Empathokinesthetic Measurement and Movement Pattern Recognition as Biomarkers for Health Status and Prognosis of Palliative Care Patients (CRC EmpkinS, Subproject D05, FP1)
summary: The aim of this study is to investigate new biomarkers for health status, symptom burden and prognosis of palliative care patients in the last weeks of life from macroscopic everyday movements and microscopic movement effects of the cardiovascular system and respiration. Health status, symptom burden and prognosis are reflected in organ and body functions that lead to movement effects and their changes during the course of life and are still assessed today by means of unstructured, subjective observations. In order to explore new ways of objectively and quantifiably determining health status, symptom burden and prognosis, this study will record data using established (electrocardiogram, motion capture method, etc.) and experimental, contactless (radar, body hull camera, etc.) sensor technology. The parallel data collection represents an essential starting point for the investigation of the innovative empatho-kinaesthetic sensor technologies which are being researched in sub-projects A01, A02, A03 and A04 as part of the EmpkinS Collaborative Research Center. On the one hand, the measurements are carried out on a healthy cohort in order to further investigate the microscopic and macroscopic movement patterns recorded with experimental sensor technology. On the other hand, data recordings are carried out in a clinical context in order to investigate the suitability of the movement patterns for clinical questioning.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient cohort:
- Patients of the palliative care unit of the University Hospital Erlangen 

Healthy test subject cohort:
- Age 18-35 years
Exclusion criteria:
Patient cohort:
- Lack of ability for contact and consent

Healthy subject cohort:
- Implanted pacemaker
- Diagnosed disease of the cardiovascular system and associated medication intake
- Diagnosed disease of the respiratory system and associated medication intake
